title: Throttle tuning laneplan and release dossier - Jun 2027 (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact lane plan for traffic throttling, the short rollout calendar for the next feature wave (June 2027), and a draft of the public/internal release notes. It’s intentionally prescriptive on throttle curves and telemetry gates so the on-call and launch team have a single source-of-truth during the 72hr window.

Scope / assumptions:
- Applies to hosted API + Dedicated pools for model v2.3 (bert-family fast path).
- We have a graceful fallback to model v2.2 quantized variant in every region.
- Autoscaler cooldown set to 180s; reserve burst pool enabled for first 4h of launch.
- Primary metric owners: latency (p50/p95/p99), error-rate (5xx, client-side timeouts), token-cost variance, request drop rate.

Quick summary of changes in this release (for notes draft):
- Introduces adaptive KV-cache prewarm for conversational workloads (reduces cold-start token cost ~18%).
- Adds a new batching heuristic that bounds tail latency for short prompts.
- Operational: exposes throttling knobs via /admin/rollout (RBAC gated).
- Known limitation: bundle-size regression for very long-context (>16k) sequences in some warmup patterns.

Mini rollout calendar (compact):
- T-7d (2027-05-25): Freeze deploy-ready branch; integration smoke tests start. Owner: Marcus Liu.
- T-3d (2027-06-03): Canary traffic (0.5%) to canary pool in us-west1. Validate p95 < 220ms, 5xx < 0.1%. Owner: Hannah Cho.
- T-1d (2027-06-14): Dry-run cutover of routing policies in staging and dedicated canaries. Observability play inspection. Owner: Rashid Alvi.
- Launch day (2027-06-15): Gradual ramp: 0.5% -> 3% -> 12% -> 40% -> 100% over 6h with throttle curves applied. Operator: Release Conductor on rotation.
- Watch week (2027-06-16 to 2027-06-22): Daily triage at 09:00 PT, retention of full traces for flagged requests. Post-launch retro 2027-06-23.

Throttle tuning lane plan (rationale + knobs):
- Goal: minimize tail latency regressions while allowing steady throughput increase.
- Primary knobs: ingress-rate-cap, sliding-window-drop, warmup-concurrency-limit, priority-queue-weight.

Suggested numeric profile (start conservative):
- Phase A (0.5% traffic, baseline): ingress-rate-cap = 200 rps/node, sliding-window-drop = 0.02, warmup-concurrency-limit = 8, priority-queue-weight = 0.7
- Phase B (3%): ingress-rate-cap = 400 rps/node, sliding-window-drop = 0.04, warmup-concurrency-limit = 12, priority-queue-weight = 0.6
- Phase C (12%): ingress-rate-cap = 700 rps/node, sliding-window-drop = 0.06, warmup-concurrency-limit = 18, priority-queue-weight = 0.5
- Phase D (40%): ingress-rate-cap = 1200 rps/node, sliding-window-drop = 0.10, warmup-concurrency-limit = 28, priority-queue-weight = 0.4
- Phase E (100%): ingress-rate-cap = 2000 rps/node, sliding-window-drop = 0.12, warmup-concurrency-limit = 40, priority-queue-weight = 0.35

Throttle escalation and rollback triggers (must be enforced by release conductor):
- Immediate rollback if p99 latency increases > 250ms over baseline AND 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes.
- Hold progression if p95 > 300ms or token-cost-per-request increases > 25% over baseline for 10 minutes.
- If sliding-window-drop > 0.2 (massive dropping) suspend rollout and shift traffic to fallback model within 90s.

Observability gates and dashboards to watch (must be open during launch):
- Latency by region and model-variant: p50/p95/p99, tail-fanout.
- Error breakdown: client-timeouts, server-oom, infra-queue-drops.
- Cost signal: avg tokens per request, model infer-time per token.
- KV-cache hit-rate: should start > 0.6 in Phase B and trend upward; anything below 0.3 indicates prewarm failure.
- Traces flagged: requests with > 500ms infer and > 2 model variants fallback.

Smoke test checklist (run during T-1d dry-run and again at each phase move):
- [ ] Health endpoints: /health (OK), /admin/keys (RBAC read), /metrics (prometheus scrape).
- [ ] Simple generation: 10 short prompts, median latency under policy.
- [ ] Conversational prefix test: KV-cache warm path exercised, ensure hit-rate > 0.5.
- [ ] Long-context stress: 20 requests of 12k tokens to verify memory path doesn't regrow OOM.
- [ ] Canary fallback: simulate model v2.3 GC spike and validate automatic fallback to v2.2 within 90s.
- [ ] Rollout-backing: validate /admin/rollout accepts throttle updates and they apply globally within 60s.

Communication templates (short):
- Incident channel subject line: "[REL-2137] Launch day alert — <region> — <signal>"
- Customer-facing note (if needed): "We are rolling out a performance and batching update to our text-generation API. You may notice transient latency differences during the first hour in some regions. We will post updates to status.redwood.ai."

Release notes draft (internal + public split):
- Internal headline: "Adaptive KV prewarm + safer batching heuristic (v2.3) — rollout 2027-06-15"
- Public short: "Improved conversational cold-starts and lower per-token cost for short prompts. Rolling out June 15; no API changes."
- Details for support ops (internal):
  - Why: Observed ~22% cold-start token cost on conversations; new prewarm reduces repeated KV misses.
  - Impact: Typical requests should see 10–20% token-cost reduction; long-context heavy workloads may observe slight regressions in rare warmup patterns.
  - Mitigation: If customer reports increased latency on long contexts, recommend toggling model-variant to v2.2 until patch.

Open questions / TODO before finalizing:
- Decide exact ramp timing for APAC regions (we are currently using same 6h window; ops prefer a 9h stretched ramp to respect overnight staffing). Owner: Global ops.
- Confirm whether reserve burst pool will be billed to Dedicated customers or absorbed by the platform for the first 4h. Finance OK to decide by 2027-06-10.
- Finalize conformance test for KV prewarm in nightly pipeline (ticket REL-2170).

Post-launch retro checklist (initial 48–72h):
- Collect flagged traces and attach to REL-2137.
- Compare actual token-cost delta vs prediction; capture anomalies.
- Update model-variant fallback timelogs and tune sliding-window-drop thresholds if false positives observed.
- Short retro notes: what worked / what surprised / immediate followups.

Appendix: Operator quick commands (for on-call)
- Apply throttle knob quickly: curl -X POST -H 'Auth: <token>' https://admin.redwood.ai/rollout/adjust -d '{"ingress_rate_cap":700}' (RBAC required)
- Force fallback: /admin/rollout/fallback?target=v2.2
- Query KV hit-rate: grafana panel "kv-cache-hit" or PromQL: avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_rate[5m])

Notes to self: Keep this doc short and actionable — move long troubleshooting steps into REL-2137 wiki. We should also snapshot the exact throttle curve JSON in the release artifacts folder after the canary hits Phase B.

-----
Document history: draft created 2027-06-01 by Sofia Patel; reviewed by Marcus, Rashid, Hannah. Last updated 2027-06-15 with numeric knob tuning after canary run.
